# FileHandle same-process transfer owner

The exact pinned public FileHandle transfer/list/deserialize hooks now consume the actual native descriptor owner. The generic registered-JS envelope still validates the whole explicit list and nested identities, serializes the main graph, detaches ArrayBuffers first, and commits hosts in the existing order. FileHandle's original close/ref checks run unchanged; no JS property copy is substituted for descriptor movement.

The private native brand is the actual FS resource class plus FileHandle kind, checked unwrap and current native async environment. Explicit native aliases are admitted by actual owner identity. A native tag/index refers to a packet-owned single-use FileHandleLease; neither an fd token nor JS pointer is encoded in clone bytes. Sidecar/table allocation precedes movement. Original public fd becomes -1 through the pinned JS hook; exposed native StreamBase fd is compiled EINVAL after the descriptor is transferred/closed, while an actual queued close remains alive until completion.

Receiver configuration retains only its own context-local real filesystem error converter. The existing internal/fs/promises registry supplies the target context's actual FileHandle constructor. A read transaction roots and reserves each native receiver before moving the incoming lease and emitting FILEHANDLE init. On abrupt read/admission, it consumes any still-state-owned lease. A reentrant init close may have moved that lease to an actual queued close job; rollback never closes its numeric fd again. Existing actual async IDs/frames/default triggers and finalization own init/destroy; the packet never carries those JS roots or source IDs. Context teardown joins work and retires port packets before releasing the local converter root.

Closed-source/destination discard, failed serialization, unread packet/Worker retirement and graph collection all use the existing owning packet/data path, whose native sidecar closes exactly once. Abandoned close failures retain a native fatal check matching the pinned TransferData close invariant; exact fatal signal/diagnostic behavior is not validated. Graph retirement runs outside graph locks. Existing worker startup consumes LOAD data after builtin and receiver setup. Musl uses CLONE_VM/CLONE_FILES/CLONE_THREAD through actual kernel_clone; kernel task creation adds a thread to the same Process containing fd_table/ofd_table. This is the guest process boundary, not an assumption about the host OS process. No kernel ABI or fork wire is changed.

This is source activation, not completed compatibility. New native FS/clone/registry/JSAPI code is uncompiled and unexecuted; material/native-reference controls are narrower. GC/OOM/realm/worker termination/close races, async provider/frame/fatal behavior and all four hosts require identified-artifact validation. Full StreamBase/private resource shapes, raw out-of-band fd close/reuse, readableWebStream and broader FileHandle/worker APIs remain separate gaps. The actual six-argument curated clone forwarder239 and consumed lease foundation are mandatory dependencies; do not apply these hooks over the earlier five-argument wrapper or bare-fd owner.
